item.text:
**Verdict**
Mixed, leaning partially positive for regime durability and external influence. The strongest 2024 evidence shows Abiy preserving regime objectives through technocratic economic stabilization and late-year de-escalation with Somalia. The strongest counterevidence shows the regime relying on coercive emergency rule, a secret security committee, and sustained repression of scrutiny rather than building resilient institutions.

**Accepted Claims**
- Title: `IMF completes Ethiopia first ECF review` | Publisher: IMF | Date: 2024-10-18 | URL: https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/10/18/pr-24383-ethiopia-imf-completes-the-1st-review-under-the-ecf-arrangement | Claim: Ethiopia met all quantitative performance criteria and most structural benchmarks, and the exchange-rate transition kept progressing with limited disruption. This is strong evidence that Abiy’s government managed a major crisis in a way that preserved state capacity and kept the macro program on track. | QIDs: 8B.9, 8B.8
- Title: `The National Bank of Ethiopia announces the launch of a new monetary policy framework` | Publisher: National Bank of Ethiopia | Date: 2024-07-09 | URL: https://nbe.gov.et/nbe_news/the-national-bank-of-ethiopia-announces-the-launch-of-a-new-monetary-policy-framework/ | Claim: The central bank shifted to an interest-rate-based, price-stability framework and added operating tools. This supports the view that the regime responded to crisis by empowering technical institutions rather than relying only on ad hoc political control. | QIDs: 8B.9, 8B.8
- Title: `Abiy publicly denied war intent with Somalia` | Publisher: Associated Press via CityNews | Date: 2024-02-06 | URL: https://kitchener.citynews.ca/2024/02/06/ethiopias-leader-plays-down-fears-of-conflict-with-somalia-over-a-planned-naval-port/ | Claim: Abiy said he had no intention of going to war with Somalia and framed peace as mutually beneficial, while also lowering Nile-dam tensions. This is direct evidence of crisis communication aimed at preserving regional room to maneuver rather than escalating into an avoidable conflict. | QIDs: 8B.9
- Title: `Ankara Declaration` | Publisher: Republic of Türkiye Ministry of Foreign Affairs | Date: 2024-12-12 | URL: https://www.mfa.gov.tr/etiyopya-federal-demokratik-cumhuriyeti-ve-somali-federal-cumhuriyeti-nin-ankara-bildirisi.en.mfa | Claim: Ethiopia and Somalia reaffirmed sovereignty, set aside disputes, and committed to cooperation. This is the clearest late-year evidence that Abiy eventually used diplomacy to convert a risky dispute into a stabilizing off-ramp. | QIDs: 8B.9, 8B.8
- Title: `Ethiopia discussing selling 10% stake in Ethio Telecom via stock exchange` | Publisher: Reuters | Date: 2024-02-20 | URL: https://www.marketscreener.com/news/latest/Ethiopia-discussing-selling-10-stake-in-Ethio-Telecom-via-stock-exchange-Abiy-says-45989643/ | Claim: The government moved a major state asset toward a public stock-exchange sale rather than treating it as an opaque political vehicle. This is weak-to-moderate evidence that Abiy was trying to manage economic power in a rules-based way that could strengthen regime durability. | QIDs: 8B.9

- Title: `Ethiopia signs pact to use Somaliland’s Red Sea port` | Publisher: Reuters | Date: 2024-01-01 | URL: https://www.marketscreener.com/news/latest/Landlocked-Ethiopia-signs-pact-to-use-Somaliland-s-Red-Sea-port-45654814/ | Claim: The Berbera MOU tied port access to possible naval use and possible recognition/concessions, and it was widely treated as destabilizing. This is strong evidence of a risky foreign-policy move that initially increased regional tension rather than preserving influence cleanly. | QIDs: 8B.9
- Title: `Secret committee orders killings and arrests to crush rebels` | Publisher: Reuters | Date: 2024-02-23 | URL: https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/ethiopia-secret-committee-orders-killings-arrests-crush-rebels-2024-02-23/ | Claim: Reuters reported a secret security committee in Oromia ordering extrajudicial killings and illegal detentions. That points to hidden coercive governance and regime defense through parallel power, not transparent institutional management. | QIDs: 8B.9
- Title: `Ethiopia authorities must stop using state of emergency law to silence peaceful dissent` | Publisher: Amnesty International | Date: 2024-02-19 | URL: https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/02/ethiopia-authorities-must-stop-using-state-of-emergency-law-to-silence-peaceful-dissent/ | Claim: Amnesty said the state of emergency was used for warrantless arrests, movement limits, and bans on assemblies and associations. This is evidence that the regime managed domestic resistance through coercion and information control, not durable accommodation. | QIDs: 8B.9
- Title: `Ethiopia authorities suspend three rights groups` | Publisher: Human Rights Watch | Date: 2024-12-02 | URL: https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/12/02/ethiopia-authorities-suspend-three-rights-groups | Claim: The government suspended three human-rights organizations while Abiy publicly praised reforms such as media freedom and NGO registration. This is strong evidence of selective punishment of watchdogs and a rhetoric-versus-practice gap that weakens institutional resilience. | QIDs: 8B.9
- Title: `Ethiopia’s leader plays down fears of conflict with Somalia` | Publisher: Associated Press via CityNews | Date: 2024-02-06 | URL: https://kitchener.citynews.ca/2024/02/06/ethiopias-leader-plays-down-fears-of-conflict-with-somalia-over-a-planned-naval-port/ | Claim: The same public de-escalatory line that later culminated in the Ankara Declaration also shows how much Abiy had to back off from an initially risky maritime tactic. It is useful counterevidence because it shows correction, but also because it reveals the earlier move had created real tension. | QIDs: 8B.9, 8B.8

**Search Gap**
- Direct public evidence on inner-circle decision-making is thin. The record mostly shows outputs: macro reform, emergency rule, repression, and diplomacy. I did not find clean public evidence that Abiy systematically replaced failed domestic security implementers because they were ineffective.
- The strongest positive evidence comes from official or creditor sources on economics and diplomacy, so it is better for showing state capacity and follow-through than for proving broad institutional resilience.
- On the domestic side, the evidence is much more consistent: the regime preserved itself through coercion, emergency powers, and scrutiny suppression, which may advance short-term durability but does not look like healthy institutional adaptation.
